title: Python widgets — Code, Sandbox, ParametricExplorer
description: Python-execution widget family running on the Pyodide worker: a graded Code exercise, an open Sandbox, and a ParametricExplorer with live sliders.

sections.title: Code — graded Python with hidden tests + peek solution

data.taskMarkdown:
**Code widget.** A CodeMirror editor + Pyodide worker + hidden test runner. The user iterates with ▶ Run, then clicks Submit to grade against the test list. Tests are hidden by default; a Peek solution disclosure reveals the reference implementation without auto-injecting it.

**Task.** Implement `add` so it returns the sum of two numbers.
data.solution:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

sections.title: Code — input + output media (side-by-side row above editor)

data.taskMarkdown:
**Code widget with `inputs` + `outputMedia`.** Both panels render in a single 50/50 row above the editor; the output panel is `live`, so once you press ▶ Run, the placeholder on the right is replaced by the figure your code produces.

**Task.** Invert the grayscale image mounted at `/inputs/input-gradient.png` (pixel-wise `255 - img`) and display it with `matplotlib`. When your output matches the reference on the right, all three tests pass.
data.starterCode:
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# The Code widget mounted the input PNG at /inputs/ before this code ran.
img = np.array(Image.open('/inputs/input-gradient.png').convert('L'))

# TODO: invert the grayscale image (hint: 255 - img).
inverted = img  # replace this

data.solution:
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

img = np.array(Image.open('/inputs/input-gradient.png').convert('L'))
inverted = (255 - img).astype(np.uint8)

plt.imshow(inverted, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255)
plt.axis('off')

inputs.alt: 256×256 grayscale diagonal gradient — black in the top-left corner, white in the bottom-right corner.
inputs.caption: Figure 1 — synthetic input mounted at /inputs/input-gradient.png.

outputMedia.alt: Same 256×256 gradient with the contrast inverted — white in the top-left corner, black in the bottom-right corner.
outputMedia.caption: Figure 2 — expected output (255 − input). Replaced live by the matplotlib figure once you Run.
